channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula aproveita maré, manda dedo, mas não antecipa vitória ante Flávio
item.description: On the last day allowed for inaugurations before the official August campaign, President Lula led a nationwide task force with centralized speeches and ministers deployed across the country. During an event, he rebuked elite criticism with an impassioned speech defending first-class rights for the poor — including health, education, and travel — and made a provocative 'here’s for them' gesture by showing the middle finger on national television. Analysts note that Lula maintains charisma and connection with his base, even in controversial moments, while the opposition remains stuck in poorly coordinated campaigns.

item.title: Pesquisas sobre batalha entre Tarcísio e Haddad levam tensão ao entorno de Lula
item.description: Recent polls show Tarcísio de Freitas is close to winning the São Paulo gubernatorial election in the first round with 47.3% voter intention, following the withdrawal of right-wing precandidates whose supporters are expected to shift to him. Lula has mobilized Haddad, Tebet, Marina Silva, and Alckmin to form a competitive ticket aiming to force a runoff and diminish Bolsonaro’s advantage in the state, as seen in 2022.

item.title: Datafolha: direita ultrapassa esquerda entre eleitores pela 1ª vez desde 2014
item.description: Datafolha survey shows that, for the first time since 2014, Brazilians identifying with the right (44%) surpassed those identifying with the left (39%), a five-point difference outside the margin of error. The poll was conducted during President Lula's administration.

item.title: Roberto Reis na Crusoé: Lula agradece a covardia
item.description: Lula arrives in 2026 weakened, with low popularity and a government that has yet to convince voters that their lives have improved. Despite this, the Brazilian right is making a strategic error by fracturing and failing to unite effectively against him, which may inadvertently aid his re-election. The author criticizes this lack of opposition coherence as a form of 'cowardice' that benefits Lula.

item.title: Lula mira diálogo técnico com Trump e tenta isolar Flávio
item.description: The Lula government seeks to keep commercial negotiations with the U.S. on a technical level, avoiding politicization amid the threat of a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, while attempting to isolate the influence of Flávio Bolsonaro, who directly appealed to Secretary Marco Rubio. Brazil’s strategy focuses on dialogue with the USTR, Commerce Department, and American diplomats to counter ideological pressure from Bolsonaro-linked factions in the State Department.

item.title: JHC tem 47,5% e Renan Filho, 42%, em eventual 2º turno em AL, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey shows that, in a hypothetical second-round gubernatorial race in Alagoas for 2026, JHC (PSDB) leads with 47.5% of voting intentions, followed by Renan Filho (MDB) with 42%. The margin of error is 2.7 percentage points with a 95% confidence level. The study interviewed 1,400 voters across 52 municipalities from June 28 to July 1, 2026, is registered with the TSE under AL-04491/2026, and was funded by TV Pajucara.

item.title: Agência Brasil segue regras do TSE durante período de defeso eleitoral
item.description: Agência Brasil announced it will follow TSE and Presidency's Social Communication Secretariat guidelines during the 2026 electoral period, avoiding institutional publicity. The measure ensures compliance with electoral law and reaffirms EBC's commitment to public communication, transparency, and democratic strengthening. The electoral period this year runs from July 4 to October 25.

item.title: Agendas, gravações e estrutura própria: os planos para Janja na campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula's campaign plans to expand the role of First Lady Janja Lula da Silva in the reelection bid, including external agendas, participation in video recordings, and creating a dedicated structure within the campaign office. She is expected to focus on issues such as women and evangelicals, having already attended meetings with these groups and sent videos to PT religious events.

item.title: ‘Fogo amigo' de Eduardo e aliados desafia plano de Flávio de moderar discurso em 2026
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro's resignation as head of PL Mulher exposed a deepening rift within Bolsonarism, driven by the so-called 'external group' led by Eduardo Bolsonaro, which is undermining Flávio Bolsonaro's attempt to position himself as a moderate presidential candidate in 2026. The group has fueled controversy through inflammatory statements—such as Paulo Figueiredo's claim that women 'vote very poorly'—and coordinated actions that damage Michelle's image and fracture party unity. The crisis is pushing Flávio back toward ideological extremism, contrary to his strategy of appealing to the center and reducing Bolsonaro's historic rejection among female voters.

item.title: Datafolha: 70% dos brasileiros defendem punição de menores como adultos
item.description: The June 2026 Datafolha poll shows 70% of Brazilians support trying minors as adults for crimes, up from 65% in 2022, while support for rehabilitation dropped from 34% to 27%. Among Flávio Bolsonaro voters, 81% favor adult prosecution, compared to 61% among Lula supporters. Opposition to drug decriminalization remains stable, with 85% agreeing that drug use should be prohibited due to societal harm.

item.title: Michelle x Flávio: mulheres do PL tentam se equilibrar em meio à crise
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro announced her resignation as president of PL Mulher to focus on caring for her husband Jair Bolsonaro and daughter Laura, following a public dispute with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Her decision prompted female party leaders to balance public support for her amid recent attacks while maintaining backing for Flávio’s presidential pre-candidacy. Six parliamentarians, including state and federal legislators, publicly praised her leadership in strengthening the party’s women’s movement across Brazil.

item.title: Entorno de Michelle vê pressão de Valdemar para decidir candidatura
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, PL president, pressured Michelle Bolsonaro to decide on a Senate run after she stepped down from PL Women's leadership, citing her comment that she might not run. Despite this, allies like Damares Alves and Celina Leão reiterated she could still run for DF, while the party began scouting alternatives. Michelle awaits the STF ruling on Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest and party convention timing to finalize her political future.

item.title: PL da Misoginia vira novo teste de força para Motta na Câmara
item.description: Bill 896/2023, which classifies misogyny as a crime, is set for a vote in the Chamber of Deputies before the parliamentary recess, with urgency approved and a tight deadline until July 18. The proposal, supported by female caucuses and center-left parties, tests President Hugo Motta's ability to build consensus in a fragmented political landscape, with voting expected this week.

item.title: Saiba como funciona o registro de candidaturas nas eleições
item.description: The candidate registration process in Brazilian elections begins with party conventions (July 20 to August 5), followed by the formal submission of candidacy requests to the Electoral Justice by August 15 via the CANDex system, which integrates data and documentation for eligibility verification. The review is conducted by different authorities: the TSE for presidential and vice-presidential tickets, TREs for state and federal offices, and electoral judges for municipal positions, ensuring transparency and security in the electoral process.

item.title: Sem comando, campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro é festival de erros
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is marked by a lack of strategic leadership, showing clear signs of physical and mental exhaustion, including repetitive pathetic dances at rallies and frequent, unexplained trips to the U.S. Analysts argue the absence of professional coordination — whether by Valdemar Costa Neto, Rogério Marinho, or Eduardo Bolsonaro — has left the candidate isolated and prone to errors that reveal desperation, not strategy. His sixth trip to Washington this year is seen as a last-ditch effort to seek foreign support to pressure Brazil, signaling the collapse of internal campaign structure.

item.title: A 90 dias da eleição, direita rachada favorece Lula, que sofre pressão de tarifaço
item.description: With 90 days to go until the 2026 elections, Lula leads in polls but faces pressure from the Banco Master scandal and the threat of new U.S. tariffs. The right is deeply divided following a public rift between Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle Bolsonaro, marked by family tensions and ideological splits within the PL, especially in Ceará. Lula has intensified his campaign-style agenda with nationwide announcements, while Michelle has publicly praised Lula’s government policies.

item.title: O que Michelle Bolsonaro não perdoa na briga com Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro says Flávio Bolsonaro did not make a sincere attempt to approach her after the video she recorded. She noticed his public gestures as a reaction to her video but sees them as superficial and not genuine. The former first lady feels there is a lack of authenticity in the stepson's effort to reconcile.

item.title: Ministro da Fazenda defende tributar mais os ricos, rever programas sociais e cortar benefícios fiscais nos próximos anos
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan advocates for higher taxation on income taxation, reviewing of targeting, as austerbate the economy over the next few years. He noted he has not been formally approached by Lula's reelection campaign but has been in talks with Gabrielli and other PT and allied party leaders.

item.title: Entrevista: Capobianco diz que 'tensão entre ministérios' atrasa mapa do caminho e cita garantias para asfaltar BR-319
item.description: Environment Minister João Paulo Capobianco explained that delays in the national roadmap to phase out fossil fuels stem from internal tensions between ministries, particularly between environmental and developmental agendas. He stated that paving the BR-319 highway will only occur if environmental conditions are met and lamented that the promised climate authority has not yet been established. The plan is expected to be released in the coming weeks, with 95% agreement already reached among the involved ministries.

item.title: Da Papudinha à domiciliar sem prazo: entenda as decisões de Moraes sobre a pena de Bolsonaro por tentativa de golpe
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes extended Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest without setting a new review date, maintaining humanitarian conditions following his recovery from bronchopneumonia. He revoked Bolsonaro's gun license and ordered the seizure of ten registered firearms, including pistols, shotguns, and rifles/carbines, to be surrendered within 48 hours. The decision also notes Bolsonaro's history of violating precautionary measures, such as cutting his electronic ankle monitor with a soldering iron.

item.title: Datafolha: 40% dos brasileiros associam pobreza à preguiça
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows that 40% of Brazilians associate poverty with laziness, up 22 percentage points since 2022, while the view that poverty stems from lack of opportunity declined from 76% to 58%. Perception varies by income, occupation, and age: employers are most likely to blame laziness (56%), while public servants are least likely (28%). Younger Brazilians tend to see poverty as structural, whereas older respondents hold more divided views.

item.title: STF faz jogo de cena após inviabilizar eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio
item.description: Supreme Federal Court (STF) President Edson Fachin has set August 19 for the resumption of the judgment on the format of the election for Rio de Janeiro's temporary governor mandate, a decision that, according to the article, is part of a staged effort by a faction of the Court to prevent a supplementary election in the state. The move is seen as a strategy to block the supplemental election, with full content available only to subscribers.

item.title: Das convenções às urnas: a três meses das eleições, saiba o que acontece até a votação em outubro
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections will enter their decisive phase from July to October, starting with party conventions (July 20 to August 5) to formalize candidates, followed by registration with the Electoral Justice until August 15. Electoral campaigning begins on August 16, with the first round on October 4 and a potential second round on October 25 for majoritarian offices such as president and governor.

item.title: Datafolha: 50% preferem pagar menos impostos a ter serviços públicos
item.description: The Datafolha poll reveals that 50% of Brazilians prefer paying lower taxes and using private health and education services, while 44% support higher taxes to maintain free public services. In 2022, the options were technically tied (46% vs 48%), showing a shift in public opinion about the state's role. Significant differences exist by gender, religion, and voting intention: men and evangelicals favor lower taxes, whereas women and Lula supporters lean toward greater public funding.

item.title: Maioria diz que depender menos do governo melhora a vida, aponta Datafolha
item.description: A June 2026 Datafolha survey shows that 65% of Brazilians believe reducing dependence on government improves their lives — the highest level since the survey began in 2013. Support is stronger among men (71%) than women (59%), highest in the Southeast (70%), while the Northeast leads in preference for more government benefits (38%). Among Lula (PT) voters, 50% agree with less government dependence, compared to 79% of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) supporters.

item.title: Funcionários da Abin defendem lei para evitar nova “Abin Paralela”
item.description: Intelis, the union of Abin intelligence professionals, advocates for the approval of Bill No. 6423/2025 to update Brazil’s state intelligence legal framework, citing the 'Abin Paralela' case as a reason to prevent future abuses. The group argues that resistance from the Civilian House, SRI, and Federal Police is unfounded and that the Abin Paralela scandal should instead justify robust regulation with effective oversight and accountability. The bill’s rapporteur is Senator Nelsinho Trad (PSD-MS), and a Senate plenary vote is scheduled for July 8, 2026.

item.title: Um título do Brasil na Copa pode ajudar ou atrapalhar candidatos a presidente? Veja o que dizem especialistas
item.description: A victory by the Brazilian national team in the 2026 World Cup could generate an emotional transfer effect, indirectly boosting the popularity of the sitting president due to national euphoria, though this impact is subtle and not rational. Experts note that while there is no conscious voting based on sports results, the post-victory contentment climate may favor perceptions of the current government. The effect is considered temporary and more symbolic than decisive for the October 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Na reta final antes de proibição pela lei eleitoral, Lula faz 47 viagens, visitas e entregas em dois meses
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva carried out 47 commitments involving trips, visits and deliveries in May and June 2024, focusing on health and agribusiness, before the electoral ban on public work inaugurations takes effect on July 4. São Paulo led with 12 events, followed by Rio de Janeiro with 8, while international agendas included the U.S., France (G7) and Paraguay. Most activities were concentrated in the Southeast, with announcements and launches being the most recurring actions.

item.title: Por que Lula mostrou o dedo do meio em evento oficial do governo
item.description: During an official event at the Planalto Palace, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva raised his middle finger while arguing that poor people also deserve access to high-quality goods and services, citing the Brazil Sorridente dental program as an example of first-class care. He rejected the idea that 'poor people don’t like good things' and highlighted other government announcements, including investments in the Agora Tem Especialistas program, R$ 206.6 million for ten federal campuses, and the delivery of 900 homes under the Minha Casa Minha Vida program.

item.title: Mulher de Ramagem pede licença para disputar eleições
item.description: Rebeca Ramagem, wife of the cassed federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem, requested and obtained leave from her position as a state prosecutor in Roraima to run in the 2026 elections, currently residing in the United States with her fugitive husband. She is affiliated with the PL party and has not yet specified the office she seeks, though she polled Instagram followers about a possible family return to Brazil.

item.title: Governo faz mutirão pré-eleitoral para manter seguidores em perfis oficiais
item.description: The federal government is conducting a pre-election sweep to remove posts from official profiles before the start of the electoral blackout period, which restricts government advertising in the three months leading up to the 2026 elections. The urgent order came from the Secom, prompting ministry teams to work quickly to comply with the regulation.

item.title: A visita de Flávio Bolsonaro ao ‘epicentro’ da crise com Michelle
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro will visit Ceará on July 10 amid an internal dispute within Bolsonarism involving Michelle Bolsonaro and the political nucleus tied to the ex-president's sons. The visit aims to strengthen ties with André and Alcides Fernandes, key allies in the state, signaling support for their political leadership and sending a message that the conflict with Michelle is 'a thing of the past'. Michelle's absence from the agenda reinforces the interpretation that the visit serves as an internal signal of alignment and an attempt to politically close a major family rift within Bolsonarism.

item.title: Direita ultrapassa esquerda entre eleitores no País pela 1ª vez desde 2014, aponta Datafolha
item.description: Right-wing identification surpassed left-wing for the first time since 2014, with 44% of Brazilians identifying as right or center-right versus 39% as left or center-left, according to a Datafolha poll. The shift is driven by the behavioral axis, where right-wing identification rose from 39% to 52% since 2022, fueled by a near-doubling of those attributing poverty to laziness (from 22% to 40%) and increased support for legal gun ownership.

item.title: Datafolha: direita supera esquerda pela primeira vez desde 2014, aponta pesquisa
item.description: Datafolha survey shows that for the first time since 2014, the right surpasses the left in ideological self-identification among Brazilians, with 44% versus 39%. The shift is driven by changing views on poverty, security, and religion, including a rise in those linking poverty to laziness and supporting gun ownership. Evangelicals lean strongly right, while Catholics are technically tied.

item.title: Oposição critica Lula por mostrar dedo do meio em discurso
item.description: President Lula faced criticism from the opposition after showing the middle finger during a speech defending quality public services for low-income populations. Opposition figures including Flávio Bolsonaro, Rubinho Nunes, Romeu Zema, and Mario Frias used the gesture to attack the government, linking it to corruption or disrespect, with Zema framing it as directed at 'decent Brazilians' and accusing the PT of successive scandals.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro se despede do PL Mulher: "Uma nova história"
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro bid farewell to PL Women after announcing her resignation as president of the Liberal Party's women's wing, emphasizing a 'new cycle' and thanking the team for their dedication. Her decision, made following discussions with Jair Bolsonaro and Valdemar Costa Neto, aims to allow her to focus entirely on caring for her husband and daughter. The resignation came amid a public dispute with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, whom she accused of humiliating and disrespecting her.

item.title: TRE manda deputado do PT apagar vídeo de Tarcísio como boneco Chucky
item.description: The São Paulo Regional Electoral Court (TRE-SP) ordered the removal of a video posted by state deputy Emídio de Souza (PT) depicting Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) as the Chucky doll, linking him to violence, femicide, and criminality. Judge Domitila Manssur ruled the content constitutes negative electoral propaganda and irregular use of AI, lacking clear disclosure of manipulation, thus exceeding the bounds of protected political criticism. The decision responds to a petition filed by the state Republicanos party against the deputy, the PT, and the Brazil of Hope Federation.

item.title: Nikolas diz que pode mediar atrito entre Flávio e Michelle
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) offered to mediate the conflict between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro (PL), after she released videos claiming she was 'humiliated' and 'stabbed in the back' by him. Michelle resigned as president of PL Women's Wing and is considering withdrawing from the Senate race in the Federal District. The rift stems from her public criticism of the PL’s negotiations with Ciro Gomes in Ceará in late 2025, though Flávio has apologized and Valdemar Costa Neto has attempted to ease tensions.

item.title: “Dedo do meio de Lula foi para os brasileiros de bem”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate for Novo, criticized President Lula's gesture of showing the middle finger during a speech at the Planalto Palace, claiming it was directed at 'honest Brazilians'. Lula made the gesture while defending expanded access to public services for low-income populations.

item.title: Michelle visita PL Mulher: “Não é IA nem papelão”
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro visited the headquarters of PL Mulher, which she presided over until Tuesday, to take a photo with the team that worked under her command. The visit followed her departure from the position due to tensions with her stepson, Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s pre-candidate for presidency. The photo was shared to emphasize that her presence was genuine and not AI-generated or cardboard.

item.title: PDT-SP lança manifesto por espaço na chapa de Haddad
item.description: On July 3, 2026, the PDT in São Paulo released a manifesto requesting a spot on Fernando Haddad’s gubernatorial ticket, specifically demanding the first alternate position in one of the Senate candidacies for their candidate, Antonio Neto. The party emphasized its history, territorial presence, and contribution to building a democratic front in São Paulo. Haddad’s ticket already includes Márcio França as vice-governor and Marina Silva and Simone Tebet as Senate pre-candidates, selected after a meeting with Lula and Alckmin on June 24.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: Renan Santos promete picanha, iPhone e Ozempic se eleito presidente
item.description: Renan Santos, a 2026 presidential candidate, promises to provide picanha, iPhone, and Ozempic to voters if elected. The proposal, shared in a viral video, combines consumer goods with a weight-loss medication, sparking debate over populist tactics and the feasibility of such promises. Though presented informally with entertainment elements, the content raises concerns about the use of material incentives in electoral campaigns.

item.title: Flávio dá parabéns para Keiko e diz que “onda azul chegou aqui”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) congratulated Keiko Fujimori on her electoral victory in Peru, highlighting the 'blue wave' as a sign of strengthening right-wing movements in Latin America and suggesting Brazil is the next target. He also expressed hope that her administration would bring security to the country. President Lula also commented on the election, emphasizing the fraternal relationship between Brazil and Peru.

item.title: Lula faz gesto obsceno durante evento oficial do governo ao rebater que 'pobre não gosta de coisa boa'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made an obscene gesture (showing the middle finger) during an official event at the Palácio do Planalto while rebutting the claim that 'poor people don't like good things'. He stated that poor people also want high-quality goods and that the government is delivering investments in education, health, and housing. The event took place just days before electoral restrictions begin, which prohibit the use of public resources to benefit candidates.

item.title: Lula mostra dedo do meio durante discurso no Palácio do Planalto: ‘Aqui para eles’
item.description: During an event at the Palácio do Planalto, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva raised his middle finger in response to those who believe the poor do not deserve good things, defending access to quality services through the Brazil Sorridente program. He emphasized ongoing investments in health, education, and housing across 12 cities, including R$ 206.6 million for new federal institute campuses. Lula also challenged the notion that health plans are a privilege of the rich, arguing their cost is borne collectively via tax foregone.

item.title: Onde assistir a Brasil x Noruega no DF: veja a programação
item.description: Brazil faces Norway in the Round of 16 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on Sunday, July 5, at 5:00 p.m. Brasília time, with the match determining advancement to the quarterfinals. Across the Federal District, numerous bars, restaurants, and public venues are hosting free or ticketed viewing parties featuring live music, DJs, and large screens to create a festive atmosphere for fans. The game is pivotal as Brazil seeks its sixth World Cup title.

item.title: EUA contra comércio do Brasil: Entenda manifestações do governo e de Flávio
item.description: The Brazilian government and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro challenged the USTR’s Section 301 investigation into Brazilian trade practices, with the government claiming lack of legal basis and the senator urging a delay on potential tariffs until after the 2026 elections to avoid politically benefiting Lula. The investigation raises concerns in six areas, including digital trade, Pix, trade agreements, and deforestation, following a public comment period that received around 200 submissions.

item.title: A nova configuração do mapa ideológico brasileiro, segundo pesquisa Datafolha
item.description: According to a June 2026 Datafolha poll, 44% of Brazilians identify as right-wing (15% right + 29% center-right) and 39% as left-wing (26% center-left + 13% left), reversing the 2022 trend when left-wing led with 49% versus 34% for the right. This marks the first time since 2014 that the right leads in the institute's historical series, with women more likely to identify as left (44%) and men as right (50%).

item.title: Em busca de votos, Tarcísio foca na Zona Leste antes do início do defeso eleitoral
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) attended the graduation ceremony of Professional Qualification Schools at CEU Aricanduva in São Paulo's Zona Leste to strengthen his presence in the city's most populous region before the electoral blackout. The event, filled with hugs, photos, and balloons, included Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB), First Lady Cristiane de Freitas, and Senate pre-candidate André do Prado (PL), who is backed by the governor. Tarcísio emphasized that the event was deliberately chosen to conclude his public engagements before the Electoral Justice ban on agent participation in such events, aiming to boost his electoral influence in Zona Leste ahead of the October re-election bid.

item.title: ‘Não sou uma sombra do Flávio’, diz Renan Santos, pré-candidato do Missão
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate of the Missão party and MBL founder, stated he is not a 'shadow' of Flávio Bolsonaro, attributing his poll growth to authentic rhetoric and direct confrontation with Lula and Bolsonaro. He reached 7.8% in voter intention according to AtlasIntel, surpassing Caiado and Zema, while Lula leads with 46.3% and Flávio with 36.6%. The Missão party, founded by MBL activists and officially recognized by Electoral Justice in 2023, aims to distinguish itself by avoiding passive alignment with established figures.
